As Catholic #4 rose to his feet, he impeded GW #15, causing him to fall. I verbally warned the players to "cut it out" and continued to officiate the developing attack, as advantage was in effect and no additional foul had occurred to that point.

Moments later, while my attention was on the advancing attacking play, I glanced back and observed GW #15 deliver a two-handed shove to Catholic #4. This action was assessed as Violent Conduct, and GW #15 was shown a red card. He left the field of play without further incident.

Minute 20 – Second Red Card (Catholic #4, Violent Conduct)

Following the dismissal of GW #15, I consulted AR1 to determine whether any additional misconduct had occurred involving Catholic #4 during the period my attention was on the attacking phase of play. AR1 reported that Catholic #4 had stepped with his studs onto the leg of GW #15.

Based on AR1's account, I showed Catholic #4 a red card for Violent Conduct. Catholic #4 reacted by shouting "for what" and had to be physically removed from the area by his teammates. He then demonstrated dissent by kicking equipment and shouting before being calmed by his teammates.

Restart
Play had been stopped inside the goal area after the attacking player lost possession of the ball; the match was restarted with a dropped ball to the goalkeeper of George Washington, in accordance with Law 8.
